label.verdict_reason: A list of test operators and glob-pattern syntax with worked examples; a reference to look up, not reasoning to hear.

chapters.title: String pattern matching with globs and extended globs

key_ideas.text: Useful unary file/string tests: -e (exists), -d (is a directory), -s (exists and is non-empty), -z / -n (string length zero / non-zero).
[[ ]] compares strings using the current locale's collation order, while test / [ ] use plain ASCII ordering.
-a and -o combine expressions only inside test / [ ] and do not short-circuit; && and || inside [[ ]] do short-circuit, as covered in the previous episode.
Inside [[ str == pattern ]] the right-hand side is an unquoted glob pattern, including extended globs like +(...) (one or more) and @(a|b|c) (match any one of a list).
ShellCheck (warning SC2053) flags an unquoted $pattern as a mistake, but that warning should be ignored when unquoted glob matching is exactly the intended behaviour.
